<reason>CON won by making the motion’s “even if” the live decision rule: a cap that cuts higher-risk borrowers is rationing, not rescue. PRO never showed a substantial group who now pay extraction rates and would still be served cheaper; after conceding lockout is an access loss and still affirming when good-use borrowers are cut with stalling ones, PRO’s remaining case was that a later revolving trap outweighs an immediate liquidity wall. CON’s moment-of-need comparison and surgical-impossibility argument answered that more cleanly than PRO’s burden-shift that CON “never proved” substitution.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s pressure then R2/closing: PRO admitted losing the only qualifying card is an access loss and still affirmed if pay-down users are cut with stallers, turning “delete a trap” into rationing the whole risk band.</best_rebuttal>
